body:
`ReadOnlyMemorySegment` held an `IMemoryOwner<byte>`, a `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` and its own start and length, 32 bytes in total, although a segment only ever uses one of the two sources. Every `IntValueNode`, `FloatValueNode`, `StringValueNode` and `EnumValueNode` stores one, so the struct makes up half of an `IntValueNode`.

This PR stores a single source object, a `byte[]` or an `IMemoryOwner<byte>`, with a start and length, which is 16 bytes. Memory passed to the constructor is split into its array or memory manager, and a new `byte[]` constructor wraps an array directly. `IsEmpty` keeps its meaning, and reading an array-backed segment still checks bounds.

## Benchmarks

The node benchmarks run the value node code from `main` unchanged, so they show the effect of this PR alone. "New node" builds a node and runs the operation once, the way variable values are handled per request. "Reused node" runs the operation on a node built once, like a literal in a cached document. "From UTF-8 text" builds the node over a segment owned by a `Utf8MemoryBuilder`, which is how Hot Chocolate and Fusion store variable values. "From `int`", "from `double`" and "from `string`" is how `ValueToLiteral` and the OpenAPI adapter build nodes.

### `ReadOnlyMemorySegment`

| Method | Version | Mean | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Read `Span` from an array | `main` | 1.03 ns | 1.00 | 0 B | - |
| Read `Span` from an array | PR | 0.93 ns | 0.90 | 0 B | - |
| Read `Span` from a memory owner | `main` | 1.86 ns | 1.00 | 0 B | - |
| Read `Span` from a memory owner | PR | 2.00 ns | 1.08 | 0 B | - |
| Create from `byte[]` | `main` | 0.29 ns | 1.00 | 0 B | - |
| Create from `byte[]` | PR | 0.29 ns | 1.00 | 0 B | - |
| Create from `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` | `main` | 0.27 ns | 1.00 | 0 B | - |
| Create from `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` | PR | 0.85 ns | 3.10 | 0 B | - |
| Copy a segment | `main` | 3.75 ns | 1.00 | 0 B | - |
| Copy a segment | PR | 1.34 ns | 0.36 | 0 B | - |

**Verdict:** mixed in isolation, positive in use. Variable values are stored in segments owned by a memory owner, so every read of a variable's text costs 0.14 ns more on the hot path. Copying a segment, which happens whenever a node is created or a segment is passed by value, costs 64% less. Creating a segment from `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` costs 0.6 ns more, but only `Utf8GraphQLOperationParser.Parse` does this, once per parsed document, so it is not on the per-request path. The node benchmarks below show the net effect.

### `IntValueNode`

| Method | Version | Mean | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| New node from UTF-8 text | `main` | 8.50 ns | 1.00 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| New node from UTF-8 text | PR | 6.93 ns | 0.82 | 48 B | 0.75 |
| New node from UTF-8 text, `ToInt32()` | `main` | 13.82 ns | 1.00 | 104 B | 1.00 |
| New node from UTF-8 text, `ToInt32()` | PR | 12.94 ns | 0.94 | 88 B | 0.85 |
| New node from `int`, `AsSpan()` | `main` | 15.87 ns | 1.00 | 136 B | 1.00 |
| New node from `int`, `AsSpan()` | PR | 14.54 ns | 0.92 | 120 B | 0.88 |
| Reused node from UTF-8 text, `AsSpan()` | `main` | 1.91 ns | 1.00 | 0 B | - |
| Reused node from UTF-8 text, `AsSpan()` | PR | 1.81 ns | 0.95 | 0 B | - |

**Verdict:** a net improvement. On the hot path, every integer variable is 16 B smaller in Hot Chocolate and Fusion, and building and coercing it is 6% faster in Hot Chocolate and 18% faster in Fusion, which only builds and forwards it. Reading the text of an existing node is not measurably slower.

### `FloatValueNode`

| Method | Version | Mean | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| New node from UTF-8 text | `main` | 8.64 ns | 1.00 | 72 B | 1.00 |
| New node from UTF-8 text | PR | 7.23 ns | 0.84 | 56 B | 0.78 |
| New node from UTF-8 text, `ToDouble()` | `main` | 29.70 ns | 1.00 | 120 B | 1.00 |
| New node from UTF-8 text, `ToDouble()` | PR | 28.28 ns | 0.95 | 104 B | 0.87 |
| New node from `double`, `AsSpan()` | `main` | 50.42 ns | 1.00 | 152 B | 1.00 |
| New node from `double`, `AsSpan()` | PR | 48.95 ns | 0.97 | 136 B | 0.89 |

**Verdict:** a net improvement. On the hot path, every float variable is 16 B smaller in Hot Chocolate and Fusion, and building it is 5% faster in Hot Chocolate and 16% faster in Fusion.

### `StringValueNode`

| Method | Version | Mean | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| New node from UTF-8 text | `main` | 8.57 ns | 1.00 | 72 B | 1.00 |
| New node from UTF-8 text | PR | 6.98 ns | 0.81 | 56 B | 0.78 |
| New node from `string` | `main` | 4.85 ns | 1.00 | 72 B | 1.00 |
| New node from `string` | PR | 4.56 ns | 0.94 | 56 B | 0.78 |
| New node from `string`, `AsSpan()` | `main` | 16.75 ns | 1.00 | 112 B | 1.00 |
| New node from `string`, `AsSpan()` | PR | 15.90 ns | 0.95 | 96 B | 0.86 |
| Reused node from UTF-8 text, `AsSpan()` | `main` | 2.37 ns | 1.00 | 0 B | - |
| Reused node from UTF-8 text, `AsSpan()` | PR | 2.46 ns | 1.04 | 0 B | - |

**Verdict:** mixed. On the hot path, every string variable is 16 B smaller and 19% faster to build in Hot Chocolate and Fusion. Reading the text of an existing node costs 0.09 ns more, which is the slower memory owner read from the table above. Hot Chocolate reads a string variable once during coercion, so the faster build outweighs it there. Fusion writes a forwarded variable into the request variables once per parent entity of an entity lookup, which makes each write 2.4% slower (9.28 ns to 9.50 ns), so the faster build only outweighs it for lookups of up to about 7 entities.

### `EnumValueNode`

| Method | Version | Mean | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| New node from UTF-8 text | `main` | 8.59 ns | 1.00 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| New node from UTF-8 text | PR | 7.06 ns | 0.82 | 48 B | 0.75 |
| New node from `string` | `main` | 4.43 ns | 1.00 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| New node from `string` | PR | 4.50 ns | 1.02 | 48 B | 0.75 |

**Verdict:** a net improvement. On the hot path, every enum variable is 16 B smaller, both in Hot Chocolate, which builds it from a `string` at the same speed, and in Fusion, which builds it from UTF-8 text 18% faster.
